== Biography ==
{{Virginia Sticker | text= was born in Virginia}}

=== Early Life ===

William Glasgow was born 22 Mar 1778 in Virginia to [[Glasgow-12 | Robert Glasgow]] and [[Barclay-56 | Rosannah (Barclay) Glasgow]].<ref>1850 United States Federal Census for Wm Glasgow</ref>


== Family ==

On 28 Jan 1802, when he was 24 years old, he married [[Montgomery-6593 | Rhoda Neely (Montgomery) Glasgow]] in Rockbridge, Virginia.<ref>William Glasgow in the U.S. and International Marriage Records, 1560-1900</ref>

They had ten children:

* [[Glasgow-1935 | Rachel Ramsey (Glasgow) Graham (1803 - 1848)]]
* [[Glasgow-835 | Robert Barclay Glasgow (1804 - 1882)]]
* [[Glasgow-1829 | Joseph Montgomery Glasgow (1807 - 1886)]]
* [[Glasgow-1936 | Nancy Crockett (Glasgow) Black (1809 - 1881)]]
* Rhoda Neely (Glasgow) Wright (1811 - 1831)
* [[Glasgow-564 | Hadassah Dryden (Glasgow) Montgomery (1814 - 1892)]]
* [[Glasgow-1937 | Celina Shelby (Glasgow) Burns (1816 - 1844)]]
* [[Glasgow-1938 | William Madison Glasgow (1818 - 1886)]]
* [[Glasgow-1939 | Susanna H (Glasgow) Stevenson (1820 - 1846)]]
* [[Glasgow-1926 | Mary Ann (Glasgow) Wright (1822 - 1852)]]


=== Residences and Life Experiences ===

'''1805 - Adams County, Ohio''' per David Faris:  "at least two of the children of Robert Glasgow, Nancy (Glasgow) McCleeland and William Glasgow, removed to Adams County in time to plant crops in the spring of 1805." <ref>Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Pr p 18</ref>

'''1808 - Wayne, Adams County, Ohio'''<ref>William Glasgow in the Ohio, U.S., Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1790-1890</ref>

'''1810 - Wayne, Adams County, Ohio per tax list'''.<ref>William Glasgow in the Ohio, U.S., Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1790-1890</ref>

'''1820 - Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio''' per federal census: William Glasgow, Free white persons - 10; total person - 10<ref>1820 United States Federal Census for William Glasgow</ref>

'''1828 - Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio''' - elected as elder: In 1828, Andrew Burns and Wil liam Glasgow were ordained elders. On July 7, 1829, the name of the congregation was changed to "Brush Creek<ref>A History of Adams County, Ohio, p 417</ref>.  Also noted: "He was ordained elder of the Brush Creek Reformed Presbyterian congregation in 1828."<ref>Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Press, Inc., 1990), p. 32</ref>

'''1830 -Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio''' per federal census: William Glasgow - total free white persons - 7.<ref>1830 United States Federal Census for William Glasgow</ref>

'''1840 -Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio''' per federal census: William Glasgow - total free white persons - 5, total all persons - 5.<ref>1840 United States Federal Census for William Glasgow</ref>

'''1850 -Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio''' per federal census: - William Glasgow, 72, b 1778, VA;  Madison, 32, b 1818, OH, farmer, RE $4000; Margaret, 27, b 1823, NY; Mary A, 9, b 1841 OH; Eliza J, 6, b 1844, OH; Rhoda, 3, b 1847 OH; Wm W, 1, b 1849 OH<ref>Wm Glasgow in the 1850 United States Federal Census</ref>

'''Underground Railroad''' - "William and his son Joseph Montgomery were early abolitionists and helped in the underground railway." <ref>Faris, David, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (Baltimore, MD, Gateway Press, Inc., 1990), p. 32</ref>


=== Death and Burial ===

William died 13 Jan 1853 in Brush Creek, Adams, Ohio and is buried at Tranquility Cemetery near his father.<ref>Find a Grave, database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/16645564/william-glasgow: accessed November 27, 2025), memorial page for William Glasgow (22 Mar 1778–13 Jan 1853), Find a Grave Memorial ID 16645564, citing Tranquility Cemetery, Tranquility, Adams County, Ohio, USA; Maintained by Ruth Armstrong Pohl (contributor 46537569).</ref>



=== Neely associate network ===

William's wife was [[Montgomery-6593|Rhoda '''Neely''' Montgomery]], and they also gave the Neely name to a daughter, Rhoda Neely Glasgow.

James Neely had witnessed the 1779 will of [[Glasgow-4027|John Glasgow of Peters Township]], who is attached uncertainly as a brother of William's father [[Glasgow-12|Robert Glasgow]].<ref name="NeelyWillNetwork">Cumberland County, Pennsylvania, Will Book C, p. 161, will of John Glasgow, dated 14 March 1779 and proved 3 September 1779; [https://www.sampubco.com/wills/pa/pacumberland01.htm will-book index].</ref> A later Adams County family-history account identifies William's marriage to Rhoda and separately identifies John as brother of Robert, Arthur and Joseph.<ref name="AdamsCountyNeely">Joyce Wilson, "Our Ancestors of Adams County," ''People's Defender'', 29 March 2024, [https://www.peoplesdefender.com/2024/03/29/our-ancestors-of-adams-county-3/ online article]. This is a secondary family-history account.</ref>

The repeated Neely name adds circumstantial FAN-network support to the proposed brother relationship. No located source identifies James Neely as Rhoda's namesake or relative, so the connection remains a research lead.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-12]] is assessed at 95% (proved). The held Faris p18 account specifically calls Nancy and William children of Robert and places their Adams County move by spring 1805. William’s 1778 Virginia origin and later Ohio family fit that particular migration, making the named son identification strong.

Compiled family history and retained quotations, with DAR corroboration reported but applications uninspected. No claim that the 1850 census names his parents.

Next useful test: Verify Faris’s cited family/Bible evidence when reviewing the broader Robert household.

Source basis already held: [https://search.worldcat.org/title/22731567 David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990); specific retained family statements and page citations identified in each reviewed pair]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
